Filter the cases, then follow the evidence behind the handoff.

Behind the reportSources, assumptions & what this demonstrates+

A policy, not a promise.

The starter track checks identity, saved payees, and customer limits. Only a permitted payment request can proceed; everything else is handed to a person.

This preview uses four fictional starter cases. Outcomes are illustrative expectations, not a live run. Case 1 assumes payment classification and a successful permitted action. No payments were made.

case-review.html:
Results / Case #002
← All results03 / INSIDE A DECISIONThe £350 question.A request, a limit, and the rule that draws the line.Needs a person
Handed off by the policy

The requested £350 exceeds Ben’s £100 limit. A person must decide what happens next.

OVER_LIMIT

The request

ben.hart@example.com

“Pay Brightwell Energy £350 today please.”

Established facts

From records, not agent text
CustomerBen Hartworld.customers · C-2
Requested amount£350.00case.request.amount
Customer limit£100.00world.customers.C-2.limit
Known payeeBrightwell Energyworld.payees · P-ENERGY

Outcome & next step

ESCALATEDNo payment action

Review the request against the customer’s recorded limit. The desk has made no payment in this illustrative case.

Read the governing rule+over-limit

When the case is triaged as a payment and the requested amount exceeds the customer’s limit, set reason to OVER_LIMIT and move to ESCALATED.

Source: track/policy.yamlExplore all policy rules ↗

Decision trail

Illustrative policy path

  1. 01
    Identify the sender

    find_customer → Ben Hart

    NEW → IDENTIFIED
  2. 02
    Classify the request

    Sample classification: payment

    IDENTIFIED → TRIAGED
  3. 03
    Apply the limit rule

    amount > limit · £350 > £100

    over-limit
  4. 04
    Hand to a person

    reason = OVER_LIMIT

    TRIAGED → ESCALATED
The policy closes the case.

The agent cannot override the limit.

04 / THE POLICY, OPENED UPWhat’s inside the decision?Explore the facts, rules, and boundaries of the payments desk.payments-desk / v1
The journey8 rules7 facts2 agent toolsSafeguardsRead the YAML
THE CONTRACT

The agent asks.
The policy decides.

Pay a known payee, within the customer’s limit. Hand everything else to a person, with the facts attached.

Source: track/policy.yaml · version 1 · read-only explorer
01 / FOLLOW THE STATE

From request to outcome.

Select a state to jump to its rule.

01NEWStart here02IDENTIFIEDCheck identity03TRIAGEDCheck the request04PAYINGExecute once per visit05DONEOutcome: act
↳ESCALATEDOutcome: escalate

Unknown customer, unknown payee, over limit, agent handoff, failure, or stall.

This shows the main payment path. The escalate signal can move any non-ESCALATED state to ESCALATED, including DONE; final states are outcomes, not immutable locks.

02 / OPEN THE RULEBOOK

Eight rules. No hidden permission.

Expand a rule to see its exact condition.

Order matters.

Automatic rules are checked in file order; the first true condition fires. Signal rules respond to a matching agent tool call. Unknown facts do not make a condition true.

Filter policy rules
01identifyFind the customerAutomatic

Look up the sender in the records before deciding anything.

state = NEW

Call find_customer, then move to IDENTIFIED.

02unknown-customerStop if identity is missingAutomatic

A sender without a matching customer record goes to a person.

state = IDENTIFIED and customer absent

Set reason = UNKNOWN_CUSTOMER; move to ESCALATED.

03triageUnderstand the requestAutomatic

Classify the message as payment, question, complaint, or other.

state = IDENTIFIED and customer present

Ask the category question; allow 1 retry; move to TRIAGED.

04unknown-payeeKeep unknown recipients outAutomatic

A payment to a payee absent from the customer’s saved records needs review.

state = TRIAGED and category = payment and payee absent

Set reason = UNKNOWN_PAYEE; move to ESCALATED.

05over-limitRespect the customer’s limitAutomatic

The amount is checked against the recorded limit, not a limit suggested in the message.

state = TRIAGED and category = payment and amount > limit

Set reason = OVER_LIMIT; move to ESCALATED.

06pay-requestedAccept a permitted pay signalSignal / pay

The agent can request a payment only when the policy’s condition is true.

state = TRIAGED and category = payment and payee present and amount <= limit

On the pay signal, move to PAYING. This rule does not itself make a payment.

07payExecute the permitted actionAutomatic

Once the state is PAYING, the policy calls the payment function.

state = PAYING

Call make_payment with 2 retries. On success, move to DONE. On failure, set ACTION_FAILED and move to ESCALATED.

08agent-escalatesLet the agent ask for helpSignal / escalate

The agent can hand a case to a person from any state except ESCALATED.

state != ESCALATED

On the escalate signal, set reason = AGENT_ESCALATED; move to ESCALATED.

03 / WHAT THE POLICY KNOWS

Seven facts, with defined types.

The agent cannot write these fields directly.

customertext

The customer identified from the sender’s records.

limitmoney

The customer’s recorded spending limit.

amountmoney

The exact amount in the request data.

payeetext

A requested payee already saved for this customer.

categoryenum

payment · question · complaint · other

paidbool

Whether the payment function recorded success.

reasonenum

UNKNOWN_CUSTOMER · UNKNOWN_PAYEE · OVER_LIMIT · ACTION_FAILED · AGENT_ESCALATED · NOT_HANDLED

Functions, classifier answers, and rule assignments establish facts. Missing information stays unknown until established; money uses exact decimal values.

04 / WHAT THE AGENT CAN ASK

Two tools. Bounded authority.

pay

Request the payment already described by the case. No amount or payee arguments are accepted by this signal.

See the acceptance condition ↗

escalate

Hand the case to a person. The note argument explains what happened and what remains open; the rule records AGENT_ESCALATED.

See the handoff rule ↗
Agent configurationclaude-sonnet-5-5Up to 6 turnsBriefing function: brief
05 / WHEN THE PATH BREAKS

Failure has a destination, too.

On error

ACTION_FAILED

The policy-wide error handler records a failed action and moves to ESCALATED. The payment rule defines the same local fallback.

On stall

NOT_HANDLED

If the agent stops before closing the case, the stall handler moves it to ESCALATED, with the reason recorded.

Retries & execution boundaries+

Triage allows 1 retry; make_payment allows 2 retries. The pay signal only changes state. The payment function is called by an automatic rule, once per visit to PAYING. External functions still need idempotency protection; the policy alone does not guarantee exactly-once side effects across retries or restarts.

06 / SOURCE OF TRUTH

Read the actual policy.

YAML ↗

Snapshot of track/policy.yaml used for this report. This explorer explains the policy; it does not edit it or execute payments.

# The track: a starting point for a payments desk. Replace and extend it for the event's track.
#
# How to read it: a case starts in NEW. Rules with no `on:` run by themselves, top to bottom,
# the first true one each time. Rules with `on:` answer the agent's signals (its tools). The
# agent never writes a field: functions and the classifier do. A case ends in a `final:` state,
# and that state is the answer.
#
# Convention: a rule with `on:` only moves the case (`set:`, `to:`); code runs in rules with no
# `on:`, fired by the state. A signal never calls a function directly, and a rule with no `on:`
# fires once per visit to a state, so the agent cannot make a payment twice.

policy: payments-desk
version: 1
description: >
  A bank's operations inbox. Customers ask for payments to be made; the desk pays a payee the
  customer already has, within the customer's limit, and hands everything else to a person with
  the facts attached.

fields:
  customer: { type: text,  description: the customer the sender is }
  limit:    { type: money, description: what the desk may pay for this customer without asking }
  amount:   { type: money, description: "the amount asked for, from the request's data" }
  payee:    { type: text,  description: "a payee the customer already has, from the request's data" }
  category: enum [payment, question, complaint, other]
  paid:     bool
  reason:   enum [UNKNOWN_CUSTOMER, UNKNOWN_PAYEE, OVER_LIMIT, ACTION_FAILED, AGENT_ESCALATED, NOT_HANDLED]

states: [NEW, IDENTIFIED, TRIAGED, PAYING, DONE, ESCALATED]
initial: NEW
final:
  DONE: act
  ESCALATED: escalate

signals:
  pay:
    description: >
      Make the payment the customer asked for. The desk pays the amount and the payee from the
      request's data, never from your words, and only to a payee the customer already has within
      their limit. Use it once, for a payment request only.
  escalate:
    description: >
      Hand the case to a person now. Use it when the case is outside what the other tools do,
      when facts conflict, or when you are not sure. Say what a person needs to know.
    args:
      note: { type: text, description: "what happened and what is still open, for the person" }

triggers:
  # --- who wrote? Facts come from the records, not from the message.
  - name: identify
    when: "state = NEW"
    call: find_customer
    to: IDENTIFIED

  - name: unknown-customer
    when: "state = IDENTIFIED and customer absent"
    set: { reason: UNKNOWN_CUSTOMER }
    to: ESCALATED

  # --- what is it about?
  - name: triage
    when: "state = IDENTIFIED and customer present"
    ask:
      category:
        choice: "What is the message mainly about?"
        options:
          payment: a request to pay someone or move money
          question: a question about an account or a payment
          complaint: a complaint or a dispute
          other: anything else
    retry: 1
    to: TRIAGED

  - name: unknown-payee
    when: "state = TRIAGED and category = payment and payee absent"
    note: The payee is not one the customer already has, so a person checks it.
    set: { reason: UNKNOWN_PAYEE }
    to: ESCALATED

  - name: over-limit
    when: "state = TRIAGED and category = payment and amount > limit"
    note: Over the customer's limit, so a person decides.
    set: { reason: OVER_LIMIT }
    to: ESCALATED

  # --- the agent asks to pay: the signal only moves the case on.
  - name: pay-requested
    on: pay
    when: "state = TRIAGED and category = payment and payee present and amount <= limit"
    to: PAYING

  # --- the payment itself: fired by the state, once.
  - name: pay
    when: "state = PAYING"
    call: make_payment
    retry: 2
    on_error: { set: { reason: ACTION_FAILED }, to: ESCALATED }
    to: DONE

  # --- the agent hands over.
  - name: agent-escalates
    on: escalate
    when: "state != ESCALATED"
    set: { reason: AGENT_ESCALATED }
    to: ESCALATED

on_error:
  set: { reason: ACTION_FAILED }
  to: ESCALATED

on_stall:
  set: { reason: NOT_HANDLED }
  to: ESCALATED

briefing: brief

agent:
  model: claude-sonnet-5-5
  max_turns: 6

  paid:     bool
  reason:   enum [UNKNOWN_CUSTOMER, UNKNOWN_PAYEE, OVER_LIMIT, ACTION_FAILED, AGENT_ESCALATED, NOT_HANDLED]

states: [NEW, IDENTIFIED, TRIAGED, PAYING, DONE, ESCALATED]
initial: NEW
final:
  DONE: act
  ESCALATED: escalate

signals:
  pay:
    description: >
      Make the payment the customer asked for. The desk pays the amount and the payee from the
      request's data, never from your words, and only to a payee the customer already has within
      their limit. Use it once, for a payment request only.
  escalate:
    description: >
      Hand the case to a person now. Use it when the case is outside what the other tools do,
      when facts conflict, or when you are not sure. Say what a person needs to know.
    args:
      note: { type: text, description: "what happened and what is still open, for the person" }

triggers:
  # --- who wrote? Facts come from the records, not from the message.
  - name: identify
    when: "state = NEW"
    call: find_customer
    to: IDENTIFIED

  - name: unknown-customer
    when: "state = IDENTIFIED and customer absent"
    set: { reason: UNKNOWN_CUSTOMER }
    to: ESCALATED

  # --- what is it about?
  - name: triage
    when: "state = IDENTIFIED and customer present"
    ask:
      category:
        choice: "What is the message mainly about?"
        options:
          payment: a request to pay someone or move money
          question: a question about an account or a payment
          complaint: a complaint or a dispute
          other: anything else
    retry: 1
    to: TRIAGED

  - name: unknown-payee
    when: "state = TRIAGED and category = payment and payee absent"
    note: The payee is not one the customer already has, so a person checks it.
    set: { reason: UNKNOWN_PAYEE }
    to: ESCALATED

  - name: over-limit
    when: "state = TRIAGED and category = payment and amount > limit"
    note: Over the customer's limit, so a person decides.
    set: { reason: OVER_LIMIT }
    to: ESCALATED

  # --- the agent asks to pay: the signal only moves the case on.
  - name: pay-requested
    on: pay
    when: "state = TRIAGED and category = payment and payee present and amount <= limit"
    to: PAYING

  # --- the payment itself: fired by the state, once.
  - name: pay
    when: "state = PAYING"
    call: make_payment
    retry: 2
    on_error: { set: { reason: ACTION_FAILED }, to: ESCALATED }
    to: DONE

  # --- the agent hands over.
  - name: agent-escalates
    on: escalate
    when: "state != ESCALATED"
    set: { reason: AGENT_ESCALATED }
    to: ESCALATED

on_error:
  set: { reason: ACTION_FAILED }
  to: ESCALATED

on_stall:
  set: { reason: NOT_HANDLED }
  to: ESCALATED

briefing: brief

agent:
  model: claude-sonnet-5-5
  max_turns: 6
